diocese: The Episcopal Diocese of West Virginia
sourceFile: "Cycle-of-Prayer-2026-2.pdf", fetched from https://wvdiocese.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Cycle-of-Prayer-2026-2.pdf. The roster's originally recorded URL (https://www.wvdiocese.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/34/files/Cycle-of-Prayer-2026-2.pdf) now 404s -- the diocese appears to have re-uploaded the identically-named file to a new wp-content/uploads path; the working URL above was found via the diocese's own current 'Spiritual Resources' page (https://wvdiocese.org/administration/spiritual-resources), which links this exact PDF.
notes: Confirmed this is the Episcopal Diocese of West Virginia -- distinct from the separately-ingested Diocese of Virginia and Diocese of Southwestern Virginia, and from the Diocese of Southern Virginia (flagged blocked in this corpus's research) -- by the cover page's own diocesan shield/seal and full title 'THE EPISCOPAL DIOCESE OF WEST VIRGINIA', by the page footer's return address 'PO Box 5400, Charleston, WV 25361', and by the diocese's own website title 'Episcopal Diocese of West Virginia' at wvdiocese.org. `diocese` is transcribed from the cover page's own full title.

This is a single-column, 12-page PDF (cover, an Epiphany Easter-date proclamation, then a straightforward month-by-month weekly list, then a reference table of fixed Holy Days, then a closing diocesan prayer) -- confirmed single-column with no interleaving risk by rendering every page as an image at 150 DPI and visually comparing against the pdftotext -layout extraction before transcribing.

The cover-page Scripture epigraph, the Epiphany Easter-date proclamation, the 'Other Holy Days & Holidays' reference table (a fixed list of feast/civil dates repeated every year, most of which are already disclosed inline via each dated entry's own `liturgicalNote`), and the closing 'A Prayer for the Diocese' + 'The Harvest is Here' page are all front/back matter, not part of the diocese's own weekly prayer-subject cycle, and are excluded from `entries` -- not a gap in transcription.

April 4, 2026 is printed TWICE in the source as two consecutive rows: 'Holy Saturday' (subject: 'For those preparing for Baptism') and 'Easter Vigil' (subject: 'For the faith & witness of all Christians everywhere') -- both genuinely the same calendar date (the Vigil is kept the evening of Holy Saturday), not a blank-cell continuation but an explicit repeated date. Per this corpus's own rule that a repeated date is one week/entry, not two, these are folded into a single 2026-04-04 entry with `liturgicalNote` 'Holy Saturday / Easter Vigil' and both subjects preserved in the source's own order.

Most dated entries print a single liturgical Sunday/day name (e.g. 'The Second Sunday after Christmas'); several also print a second, historical alternate name for the very same day on the same line (e.g. 'Septuagesima', 'Whitsunday', 'Trinity Sunday', 'Good Shepherd Sunday', 'Christ the King Sunday', 'Gaudete Sunday') -- these are combined into one `liturgicalNote` joined with ' / ' (e.g. 'The Day of Pentecost / Whitsunday').

Many entries additionally print a separate italicized line directly under the date's own liturgical name, naming a nearby fixed feast day or civil/diocesan observance (e.g. 'The Feast of St. Timothy: January 26', 'West Virginia Day: June 20', 'Diocesan Convention: November 13-15 at Oglebay Park Resort', 'Suicide Prevention Week') -- appended to that entry's `liturgicalNote` after '; ', preserved exactly as printed including its own internal date. When that annotation names a saint whose feast matches the name of a subject listed that same week (the common case -- the week's parish was clearly chosen because it shares the saint's name), the identical annotation text is ALSO recorded as that subject's own `note`, following this corpus's existing Kansas precedent (episcopal-kansas-2026.json) for a feast-day aside tied to a named parish. When the annotation instead names a civil/diocesan observance with no matching named parish (West Virginia Day, Independence Day, Diocesan Convention, Convention Weekend, Suicide Prevention Week, National Recovery Month), it is recorded only in `liturgicalNote`, not duplicated onto the (category) subject.

June 7's entry prints its two congregations on a single source line joined by '&' -- 'Christ Church, Clarksburg & St. Barnabas Chapel, Bridgeport' -- split here into two separate `parish` subjects (different named congregations in different towns), both carrying the week's own 'Feast of St. Barnabas Day' note even though only the second is Barnabas-named, since the source groups them together under that one week. Likewise December 27 lists three congregations ('St. Thomas a Becket, Morgantown', 'Church of the Incarnation, Ronceverte', 'Emmanuel, Keyser') under one 'Feast of St. Thomas a Becket' annotation though only the first matches by name; all three carry the identical note, consistent with the policy above.

The source's parish names use curly right single quotation marks throughout (e.g. 'St. Peter's', 'St. John's'); these are transcribed here as straight ASCII apostrophes. This corpus is itself inconsistent on this point (contrast episcopal-kansas-2026.json, which deliberately preserves the source's own curly quotes) -- straight quotes were chosen here for consistency with the majority of already-ingested Virginia-region files (see episcopal-virginia-2026.json). Separately, the source's own June 14 entry ('...learn and share God's story...') is the one place it prints a plain straight apostrophe rather than its usual curly one -- a genuine, if invisible after normalization, inconsistency in the source itself, noted here for completeness.

Several congregations are printed without a following apostrophe-s where an 's' might otherwise be expected (e.g. 'St. Matthias, Grafton', 'St. Barnabas Chapel, Bridgeport', 'St. Thomas a Becket, Morgantown') -- these are grammatically ordinary (the base name already ends in 's'), transcribed exactly as printed rather than normalized to match other congregations' possessive forms.

Short single-clause prayer intentions and several parish/category lines are printed by the source with no terminal period (e.g. 'All Christians who face persecution', 'The Anglican Diocese of Jerusalem', 'For those preparing for Baptism', 'The Sandscrest Conference & Retreat Center'), while longer multi-sentence intentions do end with one -- both forms preserved exactly as printed rather than normalized to match each other.

'Grace Church, St. Mary's' (January 4) is transcribed exactly as printed; the real West Virginia town of this name is commonly spelled 'St. Marys' (no apostrophe), so this may be a source typo, but it is preserved verbatim per this corpus's standing rule against silently correcting a source.

Diocesan-wide entities not tied to a single congregation -- 'Peterkin Camp & Conference Center', 'The Sandscrest Conference & Retreat Center', 'The Highland Educational Project', the Diocesan Commissions/Committees/Staff/Council paragraphs, 'The Anglican Diocese of Jerusalem' (a companion/partner diocese named as a prayer subject, not a West Virginia congregation) -- are recorded as `category` subjects, not `parish`, consistent with this corpus's existing treatment of diocesan camps and companion dioceses elsewhere (see e.g. episcopal-southern-ohio-2026.json's 'Procter Center').

'The St. Sebastian's Worshipping Community, Lost River' (February 15) is recorded as a `parish` subject (name including its own printed leading 'The'), since it is a specific gathered congregation despite not being called a 'church' or 'parish' by name.
